title: Who is pro-AI, against, or neutral in the 2026 midterms?

methodology.summary: Each candidate carries one coarse AI stance tag — pro, against, or neutral — coded from cited public campaign statements and legislative records. The tag is a reading of the public record, not a score of how dangerous the person is, and not an endorsement.

stances.pro: Public record favors accelerating AI deployment, data-center buildout, faster permitting, or opposing broad new federal AI rules.
stances.against: Public record favors construction pauses, extensive new federal AI rules, public control of advanced systems, or making AI crackdown a central campaign plank.
stances.neutral: AI-specific record is thin, mixed across dimensions, or still unscored on the main AI governance questions.

methodology.sources_note: Senate and House evidence comes from AI Congress race pages (aicongress.us) and named news interviews; governor races come from named news outlets. Undated AI Congress lines carry the date the page was read. Candidates without a verifiable quote are left off. Missing evidence is marked, never filled in.

candidates.name: Jon Ossoff
candidates.summary: Backs continued AI growth paired with mandatory safeguards on child safety, biosafety, and health care, and ratepayer protections on data centres.

evidence.quote: My office is investigating AI data centers' impact on rising power bills.

candidates.name: Mike Collins
candidates.summary: Emphasizes faster permitting, more energy supply, and business-led growth; AI-specific governance questions stay unscored in the public record.

evidence.quote: Collins highlighted the PERMIT Act and an all-of-the-above energy agenda to lower costs and spur growth.

candidates.name: Ashley Hinson
candidates.summary: Supports rapid AI adoption, rural data-centre investment, workforce prep, and China-focused export enforcement while opposing broad regulation.

evidence.quote: Those investments are creating real jobs in rural communities.

candidates.name: Josh Turek
candidates.summary: Worker and antimonopoly platform is detailed; a position on data-centre construction or general AI rules is not in the reviewed record.

evidence.quote: has not published a position on data-center construction or general AI rules

candidates.name: Abdul El-Sayed
candidates.summary: Calls for national AI guardrails, democratic control of advanced systems, and an FDA-style overseer for model development.

evidence.quote: We need AI under democracy and AI under control.
evidence.source: CBS News Detroit / Detroit Economic Club

candidates.name: Mike Rogers
candidates.summary: Backs a temporary Michigan construction pause and ratepayer protections while framing AI investment, competitiveness, and jobs as priorities.

evidence.quote: I think we need to take a pause

evidence.quote: Would require large data centers to fund needed infrastructure and supports tighter siting, cost, water, and community protections.

candidates.name: Ken Paxton
candidates.summary: Pairs a market-led energy posture with aggressive state enforcement of privacy and child-safety rules against technology and AI companies.

evidence.quote: Texas launched a dedicated initiative to enforce privacy laws against technology and AI companies.
evidence.source: AI Congress / Texas Attorney General record

evidence.quote: Paxton has touted his lawsuits against major social media companies

candidates.name: Roy Cooper

evidence.quote: Data centers should pay the full cost of all the power they use.

candidates.name: Sherrod Brown
